stageText.design: The master plan: roads, the river and its park, housing, schools, kindergartens, shops and bus stops, planned in one place.
stageText.build: Roads and bridges go in first, then the district rises package by package. Trees and green space come last.
stageText.operate: The district comes alive: lights on, cars and buses moving, people walking in the parks and courtyards — all run from one board.

system.title: System overview
system.lead: TwinCore brings everything from the city’s base data through planning, construction, monitoring and operation into one platform. Its four main parts are linked by objects with unique IDs.

site.what: First, choose where to build. The system reads each candidate plot’s size, zoning and utility connections straight from the base data.
site.why: So you know what can be built on a plot before you buy it.

bim.what: The approved drawings lie on the plot, and the 3D building model (BIM) rises from them floor by floor.
bim.why: Every model is checked against the planning rules automatically: how much floor space the plot may hold (FAR) and how much of the plot the building may cover.

finance.what: The model gives the floor area and the number of homes, so the cost follows directly: land, construction, design and VAT.
finance.why: Set against the sale price, you see the profit and the return before anything is decided.

live.bimDone: The model meets the planning rules

twin.lodTitle: How much detail the model shows
twin.lod1: The building as a simple block: its size and height. Used for city-wide analysis such as shadows and views.
twin.lod2: Adds the real roof shape and what stands on the roof.
twin.lod3: The outside in full: windows, balconies, entrance and doors.
twin.lod4: Looks inside: the floors, the frame that holds it up, and the pipes and ducts, shown with a cut-away.
twin.simNote: For illustration — real runs use the measured ground heights and the 3D city model.

flood.name: Flood
flood.desc: On the terrain model, see where the river spreads as it rises: first the channel, then the floodplain, finally the street and buildings.

air.name: Air
air.desc: Air pollution over the district: in still air with high emissions a haze covers everything; as the wind picks up the fog moves and breaks apart. The white streaks show wind direction and speed.

traffic.name: Traffic
traffic.desc: As density rises there are more cars and they slow down. Every car keeps its distance to the one ahead.

geoai.title: AI that reads aerial photos
geoai.desc: An AI model spots and counts buildings, cars, trees and other objects in a photo taken from the air.
geoai.caption: Click a type to show or hide it; hover to highlight it. Each number shows how sure the AI is, out of 1.
geoai.captionTouch: Tap a type to show or hide it. Each number shows how sure the AI is, out of 1.

control.workspaceLine: A 29-section control workspace — with sample data.

about.crane: Crane lift load as a share of rated capacity. Above 95% lifting stops automatically.
about.concrete: Core temperature of freshly poured concrete. Too hot and it cracks.
about.settlement: How far the foundation has sunk since it was first measured.
about.tilt: How far the building’s frame leans away from straight up.
about.dust: Dust in the air at the edge of the site (PM10). Over the limit, water sprays start.
about.noise: Noise on the side facing the neighbouring homes.

log.c: Crane 1: load at 96% — lifting stopped automatically
log.d: Safety: guard rails at floor edges checked, issue closed
